column1: # The listener's audibility thresholds: how large a difference in each reading must be before it is
# worth reporting. One row per reading id, or per unit as a fallback (id `*`). `rel` thresholds are a
# fraction of the reference's value; `abs` ones are in the reading's unit. The owner's own thresholds,
# from calibration (plan L3), override these rows and stay local.
# Sources: research:listening/audibility-thresholds.md (level about 0.5-1 dB; rise and decay time about
# 25 %; spectral centroid 4-5 % with pitch fixed; pitch a fraction of a percent, worse for short
# sounds). Rows marked `chosen` have no published threshold and are set against the guide's
# measurements (docs/drum-model-fitting.md); calibration replaces them. A `context` (a sound family's
# name) limits a row to that family; a `floor` is the smallest value a relative threshold treats as
